title: Protobuf: cleanup both golang/protobuf and gogo/protobuf
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Both `github.com/golang/protobuf` and `github.com/gogo/protobuf` are deprecated. 

- [github.com/golang/protobuf](https://github.com/golang/protobuf) is the first version of Go protocol buffer API.  **Deprecated**. 
- [github.com/gogo/protobuf](https://github.com/gogo/protobuf) is actually a fork of `github.com/golang/protobuf` with extra code generation features. **Deprecated**. 
-  [google.golang.org/protobuf](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go) is the second version of the Go protocol buffer API. **Active**. 

In short, **[google.golang.org/protobuf](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go)** is the future, so we should cleanup both `github.com/golang/protobuf` and `github.com/gogo/protobuf`, and only use `google.golang.org/protobuf`.

We also need to cleanup gogo/protobuf for raft.

### Why is this needed?

Same as above

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Based on findings/discussions in #17892 the conclusion was basically that we need to migrate away from these deprecated packages to google.golang.org/protobuf to be able to bump certain dependencies and be able to make use of standards they provide. At the same time there might not be bandwidth available to work on this. To kick things of at least, I took some time looking into how etcd are using gogo/protobuf as a first start to get a better understanding what's involved making this change, what it might affect and as a way to get some discussions going.

First I did a search to see if others have documented their migration and found https://thoughts.8-p.info/en/containerd-gogo-migration which includes some interesting details and links to PRs of their work.

# gogo/protobuf usage investigation:

## Extensions

https://github.com/gogo/protobuf/blob/master/extensions.md

### option (gogoproto.marshaler_all) = true;
Generates Marshal and MarshalTo method for each message
https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/gogo/protobuf/plugin/marshalto?utm_source=godoc

<details><summary>Usage of Marshal:</summary>

### option (gogoproto.unmarshaler_all) = true;

### option (gogoproto.sizer_all) = true;
generates a Size or ProtoSize method for each message. This is useful with the MarshalTo method generated by the marshalto plugin and the gogoproto.marshaler and gogoproto.marshaler_all extensions
https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/gogo/protobuf/plugin/size?utm_source=godoc

<details><summary>Usage of Size:</summary>

/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/bootstrap.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/server.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/api/rafthttp/http.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/api/rafthttp/msg_codec.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/api/rafthttp/msgappv2_codec.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/api/rafthttp/pipeline.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/api/rafthttp/stream.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/api/rafthttp/transport.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/api/rafthttp/util_test.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/api/snap/message.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/interceptor.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/watch.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/txn/txn.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/etcdserver/txn/util.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/storage/wal/encoder.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/server/storage/wal/wal_bench_test.go
/Users/<user>/go/src/github.com/participant5/etcd/tests/e2e/watch_delay_test.go
</details>

### option (gogoproto.goproto_getters_all) = false;
if false, the message is generated without get methods, this is useful when you would rather want to use face

Should behave as standard protobuf generation based on my knowledge.

### option (gogoproto.goproto_enum_prefix_all) = false;
if false, generates the enum constant names without the messagetype prefix

Should behave as standard protobuf generation based on my knowledge.

### gogoproto.nullable
if false, a field is generated without a pointer (see warning below).
Disabled for fields in api/etcdserverpb/etcdserver.proto and server/storage/wal/walpb/record.proto should behave as standard protobuf generation based on my knowledge.
Enabled for Request.Refresh field in api/etcdserverpb/etcdserver.proto, but not exactly sure how it's used?

## Migrating from gogo/protobuf Marshal, MarshalTo, Unmarshal, Size:
By switching to google.golang.org/protobuf you don't get automatic generation of these methods in generated code for messages (Go structs). 

Seems like server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/grpc.go uses a custom codec, server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/codec.go, which 
uses proto.Marshal and proto.Unmarshal from github.com/golang/protobuf.

The google.golang.org/protobuf/proto package provides Marshal, Unmarshal and Size functions, however  
it uses proto.Reflect (reflection during runtime) which might degrade performance/throughput. 

The [pbutil package](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/main/pkg/pbutil/pbutil.go) mentioned above seems like it's used quite a lot so should be quite straightforward change that to use proto package instead for Marshal/Unmarshal.

Any direct thoughts/insights whether it's plausible switching to google.golang.org/protobuf/proto package and use reflection during runtime for Marshal/Unmarshal and/or what affect it might have given that server/etcdserver/api/v3rpc/grpc.go doesn't seem to use it for request/response encode/decoding?

One idea I had was as a first step try migrating to use github.com/google/protobuf/proto where possible and see what breaks/performance degrades. Thoughts?

<details><summary>References:</summary>

https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go/blob/master/proto/decode.go
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go/blob/master/proto/encode.go
https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf-go/blob/master/proto/size.go
</details>

OK.

How about this. Depending on the dead project gogo/protobuf leads us to 2019 era crypto and a version of x/text that has a HIGH CVE against it:

```
github.com/gogo/protobuf@v1.3.2 golang.org/x/tools@v0.0.0-20210106214847-113979e3529a
golang.org/x/tools@v0.0.0-20200619180055-7c47624df98f golang.org/x/net@v0.0.0-20200226121028-0de0cce0169b
golang.org/x/net@v0.0.0-20190404232315-eb5bcb51f2a3 golang.org/x/crypto@v0.0.0-20190308221718-c2843e01d9a2
golang.org/x/net@v0.0.0-20200226121028-0de0cce0169b golang.org/x/text@v0.3.0
```
See https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2021-38561 for info about the x/text problem.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
> There is a high severity CVE that is impossible to solve without resolving dead dependencies such as this.

If the issue is in a transitive dependency, it is not accurate that it cannot be resolved without dropping gogo.


> Depending on the dead project gogo/protobuf leads us to 2019 era crypto and a version of x/text

That's easily resolved by explicitly requiring a newer version of x/crypto or x/text.

The version of those used is the maximal version required by anything in the dependency tree. gogo protobuf requiring an older version of those does not preclude etcd or k8s requiring / linking / building with a newer version that resolves an x/crypto or x/text CVE

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
That's great news that the fix is easier than dropping a dead dependency.

But it doesn't change the fact that etcd should require that higher dependency and test on that version.

Perhaps it is controversial, but my feeling is that adding the latest version of etcd as a dependency should not impose several CVE's absent undocumented work-arounds.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
> But it doesn't change the fact that etcd should require that higher dependency and test on that version.

It already does. The etcd go.mod file already requires updated x/crypto and x/text modules versions within the last few months that are not vulnerable to the CVE you linked. That is what etcd builds and tests with. 

> Perhaps it is controversial, but my feeling is that adding the latest version of etcd as a dependency should not impose several CVE's absent undocumented work-arounds.

It does not. Go's version resolution means anything depending on etcd inherits etcd's requirements for newer versions of the crypto and text modules automatically.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
I have been investigating and it looks a bit like the core of my problem is that CodeInsight seems to think that because a vulnerable version appears in go.sum due to the minimum version algorithm that there is a security problem. That makes no sense, of course. I can't find any other place that they might be even inventing that version.

My provisional course of action is to blame them until proven wrong.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
I don't think the work in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5589 intersects with this issue at all. That is focused on dropping use of gogo for non-grpc REST API go types. In Kubernetes:
1. proto files are not the canonical definition of our API, our go types are
2. we do not use the standard protobuf stack to do encoding/decoding of our gogo-generated go types
3. we've already dropped runtime dependencies on gogo (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134256)
4. we will resolve the generation-time dependencies by forking and pruning the gogo generator to just the surface area required by Kubernetes REST API types (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134530)

In contrast, etcd:
1. does treat the proto files as the primary API definition
2. does use the standard proto stack to do encoding / decoding
3. uses the resulting go files in grpc APIs

Kubernetes also had a bunch of proto-defined grpc APIs that we already just converted from gogo to standard protoc-generated types - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3Asaschagrunert+gogo+is%3Amerged

That's what I would expect here. Don't block this waiting for https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5589

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
I sketched out a possible sequence of changes in https://github.com/participant9/etcd/commits/protoc/

1. use standard proto go types / packages instead of gogo when possible
2. split grpc generation out to standard grpc + separate files
3. stop using custom gogo generation options one by one, package by package, and backfill or adjust usage after each removal
4. switch generation from gogo to standard protoc and fixup impacted code

I opened https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/21261 with that branch just in case you want to run CI on it.

Here are the categories of risks I see that need evaluation / decisions / test coverage:

changes / risks caught by compiler / vet / tests:
* protoc doesn't generate Marshal/Unmarshal/Size instance methods (use proto package methods now)
* `go vet` errors on non-pointer copies
* DeepEqual fails due to internal state (must switch to something like cmp.Diff or proto.Equal)
* cmp.Diff fails if protocmp.Transform() is not used
* grpc server interface changes (must inline UnimplementedServer to compile)

changes / risks that could impact clients that update to new library/go type versions:
* NPE risk on structured fields that changed to pointers – can use nil-safe getters, but not sure what out-of-tree clients need to be made safe there. Example:
   ```diff
    func (wr *WatchResponse) IsProgressNotify() bool {
   -       return len(wr.Events) == 0 && !wr.Canceled && !wr.Created && wr.CompactRevision == 0 && wr.Header.Revision != 0
   +       return len(wr.Events) == 0 && !wr.Canceled && !wr.Created && wr.CompactRevision == 0 && wr.Header.GetRevision() != 0
    }
   ```
* comparison risk for fields that changed from uint64 to *uint64 – ==/!= comparisons are wrong now, but will not fail compilation. Example:
   ```diff
   -                       if snap.Index == w.start.Index {
   -                               if snap.Term != w.start.Term {
   +                       if snap.GetIndex() == w.start.GetIndex() {
   +                               if snap.GetTerm() != w.start.GetTerm() {
   ```

changes / risks that need close attention to be sure we haven't changed the wire serialization:
* json encoding/decoding change in generated types - this is failing the `go.etcd.io/etcd/tests/v3/framework/e2e` (see the last debug commit in my branch), but that test looks really weird to begin with ... I don't know if the json serialization changes for proto types impacts the etcd API surface
* stricter encoding/decoding of string fields with invalid utf-8 data (xref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136323#issuecomment-3786326053)
* unintentional / unexpected wire differences ... you would want robust encoding/decoding compatibility tests in place to make sure the new types successfully round-trip with the old types
* unintentional / unexpected side-effects of known wire differences ... fields being nullable means they can now be omitted when they are zero value. I don't know if etcd relies on byte-for-byte identical proto serializations of its types or not.
* performance impact of the standard proto marshaling/unmarshaling
* performance impact of passing messages by pointer instead of value (though this might actually help performance)

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
hoisting my comment from https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/21261#issuecomment-3861363358 as a sketch of the order I'd recommend to chip away at the problem gradually and safely

---

> I think the PR clarifies a lot on the work that needs to be done, however it will take some time to fix tests and push it through review. @participant9 do you plan to finish it?
> 
> I think the etcd community could do the heavy lifting if needed. Let me know if you need help with next steps.

This was mostly intended as a sketch of the steps / order I would recommend. I wasn't planning to own the progress here.

Doing cleanups that remove unused / dead code (like https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/21263) are a great first step.

The first few layers of this PR could also be pulled out and merged as a series of PRs with ~no impact.
1. `Switch to standard go packages` + regenerate
2. `Split out grpc generation` + regenerate + add "unimplemented" grpc server interfaces
3. `Drop enum prefix gogo option` + regenerate + backfill hand-written constants
4. `Drop goproto_getters_all gogo option` + regenerate to add field getters
5. `Drop marshaler_all, unmarshaler_all, sizer_all gogo options` + regenerate

Then the layers that drop the `nullable` decorators could be worked through package by package. As long as we fully understand who is using the fields which are now pointers and make them nil-safe or switch them to use generated getters, and we don't rely on byte-for-byte proto serialization of zero-value fields, that is fairly contained.

1. `snappb: drop gogoproto.nullable` + regenerate + `use GetCrc()`
2. `etcdserverpb: drop gogoproto.nullable` + regenerate + `use NodeID() and GetClusterID()` (this is much simpler after #21263)
3. `walpb: drop gogoproto.nullable` + regenerate + `use GetType()/GetCrc()/GetIndex()/GetTerm()`

The `Switch to standard protoc-gen-go` commit is the big change that requires switching to proto marshaling, dealing with json serialization differences, no longer passing proto message types by value, etc, etc. Understanding and shepherding the results of those changes requires more detailed knowledge of etcd than I have.

We could possible do some prefactoring work we know *will* be required as part of the gogo change before switching the generation:
* Stop passing messages by value ... I'm not sure if there are performance implications of this change
* _Maybe_ switch to proto marshal / unmarshal / size calls instead of instance methods ahead of switching the generated types (or route them through a single spot that can do the switch like `pbutil`) ... I'm not sure if there are performance implications of this change

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> The first few layers of this PR could also be pulled out and merged as a series of PRs with ~no impact.

This makes perfect sense to me!

> 
> 1. `Switch to standard go packages` + regenerate
> 2. `Split out grpc generation` + regenerate + add "unimplemented" grpc server interfaces
> 3. `Drop enum prefix gogo option` + regenerate + backfill hand-written constants
> 4. `Drop goproto_getters_all gogo option` + regenerate to add field getters
> 5. `Drop marshaler_all, unmarshaler_all, sizer_all gogo options` + regenerate

As far as I know, the change doesn't change the wire format. So it should be safe. Also we have some mix-version e2e test cases to cover this. We should be good as long as all workflows are green.



> Then the layers that drop the `nullable` decorators could be worked through package by package.

Yes, we can address this as next step.


> * _Maybe_ switch to proto marshal / unmarshal / size calls instead of instance methods ahead of switching the generated types (or route them through a single spot that can do the switch like `pbutil`) ... I'm not sure if there are performance implications of this change

Most likely there is impact on performance. That's the reason why gogo protobuf was so popular. We need to evaluate the impact.

> Last time, I run into this issue and maybe we need to update client SDK first to avoid passing value.
> So scary to handle that as new contributor at 2023 😂
> cc @reporter @participant8 I think we can start to thinking refactoring client-SDK first. It's main blocker to do migration.

@participant4 not sure why start with client SDK. I think the items proposed by @participant9 makes more sense.



> This was mostly intended as a sketch of the steps / order I would recommend. I wasn't planning to own the progress here.

@participant9 do you want etcd maintainers to take over now or at a certain point, or etcd maintainers to provide help?  Eventually we (@reporter @participant4 @participant8 ) might have to jump in to help.

I rebased https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/21261 and split out the next round of things that could merge prior to switching the generator, with no performance implications:

- https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/pull/21290

See below commands to generate the diff for the root package. Other packages use similar commands. I may generate a tool/script to automate all the steps for both raft and etcd sometime later. cc @participant4 @participant9 

```
# Install the apidiff command
$ go install golang.org/x/exp/cmd/apidiff@latest

$ cd go/src/github.com/openkvlab/raft
# write export data of the new package to api.root.new
$ apidiff -w api.root.new github.com/openkvlab/raft

# The commit is the old commit right before the gogo/protobuf changes
$ git worktree add ../raft_old d49f9a050a55c07edbe682271460765fa869bfcd  
$ cd ../raft_old
# write export data of the old package to api.root.old
$ apidiff -w api.root.old github.com/openkvlab/raft

# compare the old and new modules
$ apidiff ./api.root.old ../raft/api.root.new
```
